claim.text: Retired Gen19 two-clause eager continuation policy incurs larger native solve-only time, whole-process heap operations and dynamic instruction references than immutable Gen18 when first same-signature clause fails.
claim.scope: Seven fixed native timing cases on ELF64/i686; six fixed third-party Valgrind DHAT and Callgrind cases on ELF64 only; Rust 1.85.1.
assumptions: Same frozen source tree Gen18 and Gen19 in every comparison
Same external harness, same program/query bytes and limits
DHAT and Callgrind process-wide counters are not solve-exclusive
forbidden_promotions: No full ISO/GNU Prolog language conformance
No hardware cycle or causal percentage attribution
No resurrection of retired Gen19 T2-owned optimization

specification.intended_object: Typed evidence tuple: native solve-only nanoseconds, DHAT whole-process heap allocations/bytes and Callgrind whole-process dynamic instruction references.
invariants: 264/264 strict CLI stdout/stderr/exit parity per ABI
Same SHA256 input files and query content per case across variants
PREPARE-only and SOLVE modes use same parser inputs
No source modification to frozen Rust engines
known_answer_cases: T2 first-fail R128 and T2 first-success R128

implementation.environment: Ubuntu 24.04; Rust 1.85.1 release with feature-disabled libraries; native ELF64/i686 and Valgrind 3.22.0 ELF64
implementation.live_entrypoint: Matched native Rust Instant timer around solve(); external Valgrind DHAT/Callgrind on process-wide PREPARE and SOLVE modes.
implementation.representation: Typed tuples of raw native nanosecond samples, DHAT heap totals and Callgrind Ir values

metric.name: Native solve time plus independent-instrument whole-process DHAT heap and Callgrind dynamic instructions
metric.units: nanoseconds, whole-process bytes/blocks, dynamic instruction references
equivalence_attacks: Swap first two same-signature clause successes/failures
PREPARE-only vs SOLVE matched process mode

black_box: 264 strict full-output Rust CLI differential per ABI
Full Debug result equality in 7 native cases on both ABIs
External Valgrind PREPARE/SOLVE output equality across variants for six cases
structural: Frozen source SHA checks and target ELF class verification
DHAT version 3.22.0 machine-readable JSON plus Total bytes/blocks log
Callgrind Ir event-column and summary parse
metamorphic: First successful vs failed same-signature head
fuzzing: Previously frozen seeded differential corpus, not new unrestricted fuzzing
historical: Merged Gen18 performance and 241 strict CLI tests
Retired Gen19 failed gates and Gen20 authored GlobalAlloc counters

matched_baselines: Immutable Gen18 vs retired Gen19 linked to exactly same external benchmark harness
Same target ABI within each native comparison
negative_controls: First-success T2 without extra avoided copies
controls.compute_parity: Same runner ABI/compiler release flags per pair; Valgrind 3.22.0 ELF64 only; 5 AB/BA native blocks.
controls.parameter_parity: Same source files, query goals, max solutions and max steps per case.
controls.sampling_parity: Twenty native timing samples per variant/case/ABI with three warmups per process; one external DHAT and Callgrind process per case, mode and version.
controls.data_access_parity: Program SHA256 and input text fixed per case; same corpus across independent measurement lanes.

preregistration.prediction: Gen19/Gen18 native first-fail R128 >=3x and >4/5 slower blocks each ABI; external DHAT heap blocks and bytes >=3x and Callgrind Ir >=2x on ELF64, with T3 controls within 10%.
preregistration.primary_metric: Typed region with native slowdown ratios and external heap/instruction ratios; never collapse into a universal scalar.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Twenty native samples per version/case/ABI across five paired blocks; external instrument one invocation per case/tool/mode/version; no external independent replication or confidence interval.
preregistration.kill_condition: Mismatch in ordered results, frozen SHA or ELF class; profiler format/exit error; first-fail or control threshold violated.
preregistration.stop_condition: No new ownership heuristic, GC, WAM or heap design to rescue non-passing data.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M only for bounded native time and ELF64 external profiler counts with raw evidence/controls; general/causal claims remain H.

result.observed: Both native ABIs pass 7 timing cells and 264 strict differential cases. ELF64 Valgrind 3.22.0 passes 6 cells. First-fail T2/R128 ratios: native ELF64 9.985680 and i686 8.940340, DHAT ELF64 blocks 6.240490 and bytes 10.257140, Callgrind ELF64 Ir 7.100523.
result.effect_size: Gen19/Gen18 native solve time 9.986x ELF64 and 8.940x i686; whole-process DHAT blocks 6.240x, bytes 10.257x, Callgrind Ir 7.101x ELF64.
result.uncertainty: Five paired native blocks, one external instrument sample per case/mode/version. Workloads, harness and interpretation are project-authored; external tool implementation independent, not independently reproduced scientific result.
retired_claims: Callgrind Ir interpreted as hardware CPU cycles or DHAT totals as solve-only allocated bytes
active_remainder: Independent third-party author and semantic reference implementation
